title: CHAPTER FOURTEEN. On the condition of those judged — namely eternal life, man's absolute highest end
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): The condition belonging toward those judged, into ye which they come after this judgment, unto some stands as eternal life plus beatitude, unto others death, misery, plus eternal damnation. || On ye condition belonging toward those judged — plus namely on ETERNAL LIFE, ye which embraces man's absolutely highest plus last end. Caput ye fourteenth.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN. On the condition of those judged — and namely on ETERNAL LIFE, which embraces man's absolutely highest and last end.
The condition of those judged, into which they come after this judgment, for some is eternal life and beatitude, for others death, misery, and eternal damnation.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUMQUARTUM. De judicatorum conditione, & quidem nominatim de VITA AETERNA, quae finem hominis absolute summum ultimumque complectitur. Judicatorum conditio, in quam post hoc judicium deveniunt, aliis est vita & beatitudo aeterna, aliis mors, miseria & damnatio aeterna.
